holidays.name: National Plant a Flower Day
holidays.description: A day for grabbing a trowel and getting your hands dirty by planting flowers in gardens, window boxes, or any container that will hold soil. Even a sad desk pot counts.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, popular with gardening communities and florists. The date falls near the start of spring in the Northern Hemisphere, when planting season begins.
holidays.funFact: Sunflowers, one of the most popular flowers to plant, can track the sun across the sky when they are young, a behavior called heliotropism.

holidays.name: National Baked Scallops Day
holidays.description: A day for seafood lovers to enjoy scallops baked with butter, garlic, and breadcrumbs. Cooking them gently keeps them tender instead of rubbery.
holidays.origin: Like many food holidays, it grew from food-industry promotion and social media enthusiasm for seafood dishes. No single founder is firmly documented.
holidays.funFact: Scallops can swim by clapping their shells together to jet through the water, and some species have dozens of tiny eyes along the edge of their shells.

holidays.name: Girl Scout Founders Day
holidays.description: A day when Girl Scouts and their fans celebrate the founding of the organization with cookies, badges, and community projects.
holidays.origin: On March 12, 1912, Juliette Gordon Low held the first Girl Guides meeting in Savannah, Georgia, with 18 girls. The group was renamed Girl Scouts of the USA in 1913.
holidays.funFact: Juliette Gordon Low was partially deaf, and she once said she hoped the organization would get girls outdoors and into the world of careers and public service.

holidays.name: Alfred Hitchcock Day (Pop Culture Nod)
holidays.description: Film buffs sometimes mark the date around the legendary director's work by watching suspense classics, dimming the lights, and refusing to take a shower in a motel.
holidays.origin: This is a fan-driven tradition, not an official holiday. Cinema lovers pick dates tied to the director's career for movie marathons.
holidays.funFact: Hitchcock appeared in cameo roles in many of his films, and he reportedly used chocolate syrup as the fake blood in the shower scene of Psycho.

holidays.name: Awareness Day for Glaucoma (World Glaucoma Week)
holidays.description: The date often falls during World Glaucoma Week, when eye doctors urge everyone to get their eyes checked because the condition can quietly steal vision.
holidays.origin: World Glaucoma Week is an international awareness campaign run by glaucoma associations, held each March to promote early screening.
holidays.funFact: Glaucoma is nicknamed the silent thief of sight because it usually has no early symptoms, and vision loss often goes unnoticed until it is advanced.
